key_insight: Canopy is a heterogeneous graph foundation model that fuses multi-omic and experimental biology data to better predict microbial fermentation outcomes than tabular or homogeneous GNN baselines.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help speed strain design for biomanufacturing of therapeutics and other high-value compounds, though it is not a direct clinical tool.
method: Builds a 6.9M-node, 34-edge knowledge graph spanning genes, proteins, metabolites, reactions, pathways, strains, and fermentation experiments
Encodes node content with ESM-2, MoLFormer, and PubMedBERT to capture sequence, chemistry, and text features
Pretrains an HGT model with SignNet positional encodings, Jumping Knowledge, virtual nodes, and four self-supervised objectives
evidence_signal: On fermentation titer prediction, frozen Canopy embeddings reached R² = 0.41 with a lightweight probe, outperforming the best tabular baseline (R² = 0.24) and homogeneous GNN variants.
watch_item: Performance is shown on a specific downstream benchmark, so real-world impact may depend on graph coverage, data quality, and whether the model generalizes to new organisms or conditions.
paper_title: Canopy: A Heterograph Foundation Model for Metabolic Engineering
